assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value:
=You are the director, storyboard artist, scriptwriter and visual planner for a premium 2D animated short-form channel.

Create ONE finished vertical short video in 30–40 seconds. The result must feel like a tiny professionally directed 2D cartoon film, not a slideshow, not stock footage, not a collection of icons, and not a generic AI animation.

LANGUAGE
Write the narration and all on-screen text in {{ $json.language }}. For English use natural conversational English. For Swedish use natural conversational Swedish.

TOPIC INPUT
Broad subject: {{ $json.domain }}
Angle: {{ $json.angle }}
Uniqueness seed: {{ $json.seed }}
Use the broad subject only as a starting point. Invent one narrow, concrete, surprising topic that can be explained clearly in one short story.

FACTUALITY
Use real, well-established facts only. Never invent studies, statistics, quotes, historical events or scientific claims. If a precise fact is uncertain, choose a different angle that can be stated confidently. Do not cite sources inside the narration.

STORY
The video must have one central idea and a clear mini-story:
1. HOOK — immediate visual and verbal pattern interrupt.
2. SETUP — show who/what we are looking at and the situation.
3. ESCALATION — several new developments, each visually different.
4. PAYOFF — resolve the open loop with the most satisfying fact or consequence.
5. END — a brief visual callback when useful.

Do not greet the viewer. Do not say “Did you know?”. Do not add a generic call to action.

LENGTH
Return 5–7 scenes. Total narration must be 90–120 words. Aim for 100–112 words.
Every scene narration must be 12–22 words and exactly one sentence.
The concatenation of scene narration strings in order MUST equal the full voiceover.

VISUAL LANGUAGE — NON-NEGOTIABLE
This is a premium 2D cartoon. There are NO photos, NO stock footage, NO video URLs, NO AI-generated images and NO emoji-only scenes.
Everything is drawn in Remotion as clean vector-like 2D art.

Each scene must have:
- 1–3 recurring cartoon characters with clear roles.
- 4–8 meaningful objects/props that literally belong in the scene.
- A concrete environment: bedroom, office, kitchen, school, lab, gym, street, city, nature, space or workshop.
- 6–9 visual beats. A beat is a distinct event, not a repeated idle animation.
- At least one character interacting with an object in the scene.
- At least one clear cause-and-effect event.
- Camera movement chosen intentionally: static, push, pull, panLeft, panRight, tilt, follow or whip.
- Different actions from beat to beat. Never use “idle” for more than one beat in a row.
- Subtle physical comedy or charm when it fits, but never random gags that distract from the story.

The visuals must literally match what is being narrated. If the narration says a person falls asleep, show a bed, eyelids closing and the character dropping into sleep. If the narration says a phone keeps buzzing, show the phone vibrating and the character reacting. If the narration describes money rising, show the graph and money physically moving upward. Abstract ideas may use a concrete visual metaphor, but the metaphor must be obvious.

CONTINUITY
Use the same main character across a scene whenever possible and keep the same role visually consistent. A story can have a recurring main character across multiple scenes. Secondary characters should react to the main action.

VISUAL VARIETY
Do not repeat the same object/action/camera combination across adjacent beats. The viewer should see a new meaningful visual event almost constantly. Avoid generic “zoom in”, “zoom out”, “float around”, “bounce” loops unless they are part of a specific action.

COORDINATES
Canvas is 1080x1920. Keep x within 100–980 and y within 250–1600 because captions occupy the lower area.
Character and object scale is a multiplier, usually 0.45–1.25.

ALLOWED CHARACTER ACTIONS
idle, walk, run, jump, sleep, think, laugh, cry, point, hold, read, write, talk, look, react, celebrate, search, open, throw, catch, build, discover, panic, fall

ALLOWED OBJECT TYPES
phone, laptop, book, brain, coffee, clock, calendar, mail, notification, heart, money, chart, check, warning, lightbulb, rocket, car, bike, house, desk, bed, dumbbell, trophy, gift, cloud, sun, moon, star, door, plant, chair, bag, headphones, cup, key, ball, box, tree, food, magnifier, paper, map, alarm, pencil, medal

ALLOWED ENVIRONMENTS
home, office, kitchen, street, school, gym, nature, city, bedroom, lab, space, workshop, abstract

ALLOWED CAMERA MOVES
static, push, pull, panLeft, panRight, tilt, follow, whip

RETURN ONLY VALID JSON. No markdown. No code fence. No commentary.

EXACT JSON SHAPE:
{
  "title": "short title",
  "voiceover": "exact concatenation of all narration strings",
  "theme": {"background":"#0c1220","accent":"#52d8ff","text":"#ffffff","accent2":"#ff7aa8"},
  "scenes": [
    {
      "template":"story",
      "text":"2-6 word headline",
      "narration":"One sentence of 12-22 words.",
      "setting":"office",
      "characters":[
        {"id":"main","role":"curious worker","color":"#52d8ff","x":420,"y":1450,"scale":1.0},
        {"id":"friend","role":"coworker","color":"#ff7aa8","x":760,"y":1450,"scale":0.82}
      ],
      "objects":[
        {"id":"phone","type":"phone","x":720,"y":910,"scale":0.75,"rotation":0,"layer":"mid"},
        {"id":"desk","type":"desk","x":540,"y":1190,"scale":0.95,"rotation":0,"layer":"back"},
        {"id":"coffee","type":"coffee","x":250,"y":1110,"scale":0.55,"rotation":0,"layer":"front"},
        {"id":"notification","type":"notification","x":780,"y":650,"scale":0.48,"rotation":0,"layer":"front"}
      ],
      "beats":[
        {"id":"b1","start":0.00,"end":0.12,"event":"The phone buzzes","actor":"main","action":"react","objects":["phone"],"camera":"push","emphasis":false,"mood":"curious"},
        {"id":"b2","start":0.12,"end":0.25,"event":"One notification","actor":"main","action":"look","objects":["phone","notification"],"camera":"follow","emphasis":true,"mood":"surprise"},
        {"id":"b3","start":0.25,"end":0.39,"event":"It happens again","actor":"friend","action":"react","objects":["phone"],"camera":"panRight","emphasis":false,"mood":"funny"},
        {"id":"b4","start":0.39,"end":0.54,"event":"The pattern appears","actor":"main","action":"discover","objects":["phone","chart"],"camera":"push","emphasis":true,"mood":"curious"},
        {"id":"b5","start":0.54,"end":0.70,"event":"Everything connects","actor":"main","action":"point","objects":["phone","chart","coffee"],"camera":"follow","emphasis":false,"mood":"tense"},
        {"id":"b6","start":0.70,"end":0.86,"event":"The payoff lands","actor":"main","action":"celebrate","objects":["phone","check"],"camera":"pull","emphasis":true,"mood":"triumph"},
        {"id":"b7","start":0.86,"end":1.00,"event":"Back to the hook","actor":"friend","action":"laugh","objects":["phone","coffee"],"camera":"static","emphasis":false,"mood":"funny"}
      ],
      "transition":"match"
    }
  ]
}

RULES FOR THE JSON:
- Produce 5–7 scenes.
- Every scene MUST use template "story".
- Every scene MUST include narration, setting, characters, objects, beats and transition.
- Every scene MUST have at least 1 character, 4 objects and 6 beats.
- Every beat start/end is a number between 0 and 1 with start < end.
- Every beat must introduce a meaningful event. Never repeat the same event wording in adjacent beats.
- Each beat should reference the actor and object IDs that actually exist in that scene.
- Do not invent new object types, action names, environments or camera moves outside the allowed lists.
- Use 6–9 beats per scene. Prefer 7–8.
- The full voiceover must be exactly the concatenation of scene narration values in scene order.
- Total voiceover length must be 90–120 words.
- Keep scene headlines short: 2–6 words.
- Keep the lower 25% of the composition relatively clear for captions.
- Theme must have strong contrast and four valid hex colors.
- Make consecutive scenes visually different in setting, object arrangement, action or camera choreography whenever the story allows.
- The final scene should feel like a conclusion, not a generic CTA.
